subject: Civil Engineering
title: Seismic Waves: P, S, and Surface
description: A 60-second lesson on Seismic Waves: P, S, and Surface.

hook.text: An earthquake sends three types of waves through the Earth — each one shakes differently.

buildup.text: P-waves arrive first — they compress and expand the ground like sound waves in air.

discovery.text: S-waves arrive second — they shake the ground side to side and are more damaging.

twist.text: Surface waves arrive last but cause the most damage — they roll the ground like ocean swells.

climax.text: Early warning systems detect fast P-waves to warn of destructive S-waves seconds before they hit.

punchline.text: The first wave warns you. The second wave shakes you. The third destroys.

quiz.question: Why are S-waves generally more damaging to buildings than P-waves?
options: S-waves travel faster and hit buildings with more force
S-waves shake the ground side to side, which buildings resist poorly
S-waves carry more heat energy that weakens building materials

details.summary: Seismic waves include body waves that travel through the Earth and surface waves that travel along the surface. P-waves compress rock like a spring and arrive first. S-waves shake rock side to side and arrive second.
details.whyItMatters: Different wave types cause different building motions. S-waves and surface waves produce the horizontal shaking most damaging to structures, making their characteristics critical for engineering design.
takeaways: P-waves are compressional, travel fastest, and arrive first at any location
S-waves are shear waves that shake the ground sideways, causing most structural damage
Surface waves have the largest amplitude and cause the most ground damage

faq.question: Why are S-waves more damaging to buildings than P-waves?
faq.answer: S-waves produce horizontal shaking that pushes buildings sideways, creating the most dangerous loading condition for structures. Buildings resist gravity loads vertically but are much more vulnerable to lateral forces.

faq.question: How do earthquake early warning systems use the difference between wave speeds?
faq.answer: P-waves travel about 1.7 times faster than damaging S-waves. Sensors detect the faster P-wave arrival and alert areas further from the fault before the destructive S-waves arrive.
